title: Contract-first versioning and deprecation SLA for serving runtime
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Objective: define a contract-first semantic versioning and deprecation SLA for the serving runtime that minimizes surprise for customers and enables safe, auditable rollouts across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. This ticket captures the policy, the enforcement checks, and the accompanying upgrade tooling required to operate a multi-channel LTS strategy.

Principles and high-level rules:
- Contract-first: Any public surface (HTTP API, SDK behaviors, feature flags exposed to customers, config schema, auth hooks) must have an explicit contract document stored in the repo. Changes are allowed only if the change is classified and approved by the contract owner.
- Semantic increments: follow semver with additional runtime conventions: MAJOR = breaking contract change affecting client compatibility; MINOR = additive public features or non-breaking behavior changes; PATCH = bug fixes and performance improvements that do not change observable behaviors.
- Compatibility classification: every change must include one of three compatibility labels: strict-compatible, compatible-with-migration, breaking. A machine-readable compatibility header is required in the changelog entry.
- Deprecation SLA: for 'compatible-with-migration' changes that remove or rename APIs, vendors must provide a 90-day deprecation window for Hosted customers, 180 days for Dedicated, and 365 days guidance for Private/offline deployments. Emergency removals are allowed only behind documented security or legal incidents and require Exec sign-off and a public advisory.
- LTS channel mapping: maintain two LTS channels (LTS-stable and LTS-secure). LTS-stable accepts MINORs and PATCHes that pass compatibility gates. LTS-secure only accepts security PATCHes and critical fixes. MAJOR changes are released on a non-LTS track and must pass an extended migration runway.

Rollout gates and automation:
- Pre-merge gates: changelog-validator CI checks for compatibility header, existing contract doc link, and automated client compatibility tests.
- Canary stage: every non-PATCH release is automatically routed to a canary fleet (1% traffic) for 48 hours; telemetry must show no client errors or regression signals.
- Progressive ramp: if canary is clean, use automated ramp steps (1% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100%) with rollback hooks. Each ramp step requires no new errors above baseline for 30 minutes.
- Trace-based rollback: alerting hooks trigger immediate rollback on increase in request error-rate, spike in token latency, or model quality degradation tied to production prompts.
- Emergency rollback token: releases include an immutable rollback token and a documented command to rollback within 15 minutes.

Upgrade tooling and developer experience:
- compat-checker CLI: local tool to run runtime-change tests against a matrix of client SDK versions and configuration permutations. Must be runnable in CI and produce a machine-readable compatibility report.
- migration-assistant: interactive tool (CLI + optional web UI) that scans customer's configuration and flags known incompatibilities and automatic mitigation steps.
- changelog-schema: enforce a machine-readable changelog (YAML) with fields: change_id, author, compatibility, affected_endpoints, migration_steps, deprecation_deadline. CI enforces presence.
- version-adviser: lightweight service that returns the recommended runtime version for a given tenant based on their configuration, pinned model features, and stability requirements.

Governance and process:
- Contract owner model: assign an owner for each public contract; owners approve compatibility classification and public advisories.
- Review board for MAJORs: any MAJOR bump requires a cross-functional release review (Eng, Product, Security, Customer Success) with documented migration plan.
- Telemetry and post-release evaluation: collect upgrade telemetry (failed upgrades, rollback frequency, customer-reported issues) and publish a monthly compatibility health dashboard.

Acceptance criteria:
- RFC doc checked into repo under docs/release/contract-first-versioning.md (with examples and compatibility header schema).
- changelog-validator implemented in CI and green on a sample MINOR and PATCH PR.
- compat-checker prototype available and run in CI matrix for one representative change.
- migration-assistant spec published and initial CLI alpha released.

Notes / trade-offs captured:
- Longer deprecation windows for Private deployments increase operational burden for runtime team but are needed for regulated customers.
- Machine-readable changelogs add friction to contributors; mitigated by templates and CI autofixes.
- Conservative default classification ('compatible-with-migration') recommended when in doubt to avoid accidental breaking changes.

Next steps (short-term):
- Publish RFC and circulate to RT, SDK, and Security teams for review (owner: Aisha).
- Implement changelog validator CI job (owner: Marco).
- Prototype compat-checker integration with CI (owner: Riya Patel).
